artists.biography:
"The Anchoress is the Welsh multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and author Catherine Anne Davies (aka Catherine AD).
The Anchoress is the stage name of Welsh musician/songwriter Catherine Anne Davies, who also records under the nom de plume Catherine A.D. A self-taught multi-instrumentalist, chanteuse, and singer/songwriter specializing in a heady blend of gothic chamber pop and dark atmospheric art rock, Davies has drawn comparisons to PJ Harvey, Nick Cave, Anna Calvi, My Brightest Diamond, and Kate Bush. She issued a series of well-received independently released EPs before switching over to the Anchoress moniker in 2014 and issuing the single "One for Sorrow.. ~ James Christopher Monger
From March to Dec 2015, Davies performed in Simple Minds' live band, contributing additional guitar and keyboards. She met Jim Kerr through The Dark Flowers collective. She has also performed live with Ed Harcourt at Glastonbury Festival, as well as Martha Wainwright.
Davies has been described by NPR's Ann Powers as "Wales's (much more explicitly feminist) answer to Lana Del Rey."

perplexity.description:
Confessions of a Romance Novelist is the debut album by Welsh multi-instrumentalist and producer Catherine Anne Davies, known as The Anchoress, released in January 2016 on the Kscope label. The album is rooted in rock but distinguished by its sophisticated, layered production and a conceptual approach that deconstructs traditional ideas of love and romance. Each track is performed from the perspective of a different character, creating a narrative complexity that blends feminist themes with emotional and sensual exploration. Musically, it combines atmospheric textures with sharp songwriting, drawing comparisons to artists like Bat For Lashes and incorporating elements of prog and pop with a dark, introspective edge.

In the context of The Anchoress's discography, this album marked a strong and critically acclaimed debut, establishing her as a compelling new voice in contemporary rock. It received widespread praise for its intelligence, emotional depth, and production quality, earning accolades such as inclusion in The Sunday Times and The Guardian’s Albums of the Year lists, HMV’s Welsh Album of the Year, and nominations for the Welsh Music Prize. The album’s reception highlighted Davies’s skillful fusion of storytelling and musical craftsmanship, setting a high standard for her subsequent work and securing her reputation within the progressive and art rock scenes.
